kb_arrival.description:
Everyone who comes through this gate gets written into the Codex, and I've written you in. When you leave I'll ask what you're taking out with you, so keep track of anything you pick up in the cavern.

Go up the main walkway to the Long Shelf. It's the second gallery, the wide one with the open square in the middle. The inn and the traders are up there, and people will want to meet you. Come back and tell me when you've had a look round.
kb_arrival.accept_text: The inn does a decent stew. Tell them the gate sent you and they might give you a second bowl.
kb_arrival.turn_in_text:
Good, you found it. You're the four hundred and tenth person through this gate since we came down three years ago.

People here will be polite to you, but some of them won't know what to make of you yet. You arrived on this world the same year we arrived in this cavern, and a few of them find that strange. Give them time, and keep coming back.

kb_enchanter_debt.description:
The crystal down here gives off so much arcane power that I haven't had to use my own in two years. I don't know where it comes from, and that worries me.

The Shard Diviners in the Lattice draw on it the same way I do. I need a good few of them dead and some of their cores on my bench. I want to leave the cores on my bench overnight and see whether they keep drawing power when nobody's using them.

The Lattice is north-east of the gate, past the Sporefall.
kb_enchanter_debt.accept_text: Bring the cores in a lead-lined box if you can find one. I don't want them drawing on you.
kb_enchanter_debt.turn_in_text:
I left them on the bench all night and they kept drawing power the whole time. Whatever is putting it out isn't asking for anything back.

I'd still like to know what happens if it stops.

kb_index_failing.description:
Every find in this cavern gets a number and a heading in the Codex. Forty-one of them don't fit under any heading we have, and that number keeps going up.

Two of them are bothering me most. The revenants in the Weeping Colonnade carry pieces of worked Dalaran stone, and nobody ever brought Dalaran stone down here. The sentries and diviners in the Lattice carry crystal cores that look cut, not grown. I want a few of each on my bench so I can compare them.

The Colonnade is south of the gate. The Lattice is north-east.
kb_index_failing.accept_text: Bring them in separate bags. I don't want any dust from one getting on the other.
kb_index_failing.turn_in_text:
Look at the edges on these. The fragments and the cores were both cut, and whatever cut them did it in one pass without any mistakes. I think they were made the same way.

That means I'll need a new heading in the Codex, and I don't know what to call it yet. This will keep me busy for a while.

kb_naturalist_funding.description:
I've asked the Codex to let me survey the fungus four times now, and they've said no every time. They have it written down as scenery.

I think every bit of fungus in this cavern is one living thing, growing under all of it, this town included. If I can show the threads from different places are the same organism, they'll have to listen.

The Mycelial Husks out in the Mycelial Reach, south-west of the gate, carry live threads. Bring me a good handful. If you can, take them from husks in different parts of the Reach.
kb_naturalist_funding.accept_text: Label each handful with where you took it. Without that, it's only string.
kb_naturalist_funding.turn_in_text:
They're all the same organism, every one of them. This town is sitting on top of it.

I'll write it up for the Codex tonight. They'll probably make me write it twice.

kb_pages.description:
We're running out of paper. Everything we write on had to be carried down here, and there are no trees in this cavern. The fungus won't press into anything you can write on, I've tried.

Frostpine makes good pages. It grows up on the surface, and the nearest place is Eastern Hillsbrad, back up the way you came in. Cut the wood, plane it, and press as many sets of pages as I need. Press them somewhere warm. Pages pressed in the cold crack, and we lost four months of field notes that way.
kb_pages.accept_text: Press them flat and stack them dry. I'll count every sheet, so don't skimp.
kb_pages.turn_in_text:
That's about three weeks of work for the Archive, so these help a lot. I've been asking people to write smaller.

It's a long way up for a handful of pages, and you went anyway.

kb_reagents.description:
For three years every herb I've picked down here has tested stronger than the same herb picked on the surface. I don't know why, and nobody in the Codex believes me.

I need a fair test. Brew me some Elixirs of Arcane Fury, and use herbs you pick in this cavern yourself, not anything from my shelves. Arcane Fury is hard to get right. If it comes out at full strength from Underdark herbs, then it isn't me or my stock making the difference, it's something about this place.
kb_reagents.accept_text: Write down where you picked each herb. I'll want to show the Codex exactly.
kb_reagents.turn_in_text:
Every one of them came out at full strength, and this one is stronger than it should be. That's what I've been seeing for three years.

I'll take these up to the Codex-Master myself this time.

kb_sealed_entry.description:
Everyone in the Bastion has an entry in the Codex, and we keep adding to them. I've never closed one. I'd like to close yours, and seal it, because of what you've done down here.

Bring me something from each of the places you've been. Worked fragments from the revenants in the Weeping Colonnade, south of the gate. Druses from the Druse Crawlers in the Hollow Geode, east past the Lattice. Leaves from the Shelf-Grown in the Deep Bloom, whose door is in the Dim Reaches to the south-west.

And press some frostpine pages yourself for the entry. The Archive can't spare the paper.
kb_sealed_entry.accept_text: Bring the best of each, not the first you find. This goes in the record for good.

kb_sentinel_wager.description:
The floor of the Codex Hall was cut from stone we quarried in the Dim Reaches. For the last month it's been cold, and only along the lines where the stones were laid. The air in the hall is fine. It's the stone that's cold.

I want to know if it's still connected to where it came from. The Dim-Walkers out in the Dim Reaches leave a residue behind. Bring me some scrapings of it and I'll see if it does the same thing.

The Dim Reaches are the dark corner in the far south-west of the cavern. Take a light and go further in than the edge.
kb_sentinel_wager.accept_text: Bring a light you trust. The dark out there takes the edge off a lantern quicker than you'd think.

kb_the_question.description:
I'd like you to go and stand in the Weeping Colonnade. It's south of the gate, and it's full of Dalaran stonework that nobody brought down here. While you're there, bring me some worked fragments from the revenants.

When you come back I want to ask you something. You came to this world three years ago, and we came down here the same year, when this cavern first opened. I want to know whether the Colonnade feels to you like something we found, or something that was left here for whoever came first.
kb_the_question.accept_text: Take your time out there. I'd rather have a slow answer than a polite one.

ud_archive_deeper.description:
You're in the record now, which is the only reason we're having this conversation.

Go to the lower cut, past the shoring, where the Archive stops being masonry and starts being whatever the masonry was built into. Bring me more slips off the revenants down there, and put your own eyes on the face.

I'll tell you what I told the last one. Don't read them in there. Bring them up first.
ud_archive_deeper.accept_text: Keep the slips face down in your pack until you're out. I mean that.
ud_archive_deeper.turn_in_text:
You read one in there. Everybody does, and nobody admits it.

They're all addressed to a reader. Not a filer or an archivist, but a reader, one person, who hasn't arrived yet. We've been assuming for three years that we're the audience.

ud_archive_dig.description: I shift rock, and the Codex files what comes out of it. What came out last week has been crated, sealed and entered in the register, and the entry has a note in the Codex-Master's own hand saying it travels by hand and not by porter. Take it straight up the spine to the Codex Hall and into Codex-Master Ilarien's hands, and don't give it to the Adjutant on the way. I'm not going to tell you what's in it, because I wasn't told. What I can tell you is that I dug it out, it was already catalogued, and the tag on it was tied by somebody with fingers.
ud_archive_dig.accept_text: Carry it level. Whatever's inside shifted once when I lifted it, and I didn't like the sound.
ud_archive_dig.turn_in_text:
You got it there, then.

She signed for it without opening it, which means she already knew what it was, which means somebody told her before I did.

ud_archive_interlopers.description:
Get the Syndicate Interlopers out of the Archive precinct. They aren't explorers and they aren't looking for anything in particular. They're looking for whatever we've already dug up, which saves them the digging.

They came down a hole in the Alterac foothills for the same reason we did, and I'm aware of how that sounds. We catalogue what we take, and they don't. I won't pretend that's a large difference, but it's the one I've got.
ud_archive_interlopers.accept_text: If they've got anything of ours on them, bring it back. I'll want to log what they took.
ud_archive_interlopers.turn_in_text:
That's them out of the precinct.

We arrived three years ago with no more claim than they have, and everybody here knows it. We write things down. It's a thin moral position, and I'd thank you not to test it.

ud_archive_unissued.description: You read the slip again. It's Codex stock, on their paper, in their ink and their hand. It carries a catalogue number in the Codex's own sequence and a one-line description of an object you're fairly sure doesn't exist. The number is four hundred ahead of anything the Codex has issued, and the paper is new. The revenants in the Sunken Archive carry more of them, though not all of them, and somebody at the Bastion is going to have to explain how their own catalogue is running ahead of their dig.
ud_archive_unissued.accept_text: You fold the slip along its crease and put it away carefully.
ud_archive_unissued.turn_in_text:
These slips have numbers all ahead of my sequence, and before you ask me whose hand it is, yes, I recognise it.

I'm not going to say. Not until I've been down to the Bloom myself, and I've been putting that off for eleven months.

ud_bloom_argument.description:
Bring me husks from the Reach, and the thread they're strung on, and I want the thread live. Cut it and bag it before it dries.

I'm going to tell you what I'll do with it, because the Codex-Master won't. I'm going to show it to the Hall and point out that it runs from the Reach to the Bastion's own cellars. Then I'll ask her again about the burning, and she'll say no again.
ud_bloom_argument.accept_text: Bag the thread wet and seal it tight. If it dries on the way, she'll say it was always dead.
ud_bloom_argument.turn_in_text:
She said no. Of course she said no. I want you to hear it exactly as she said it. She said a thing which has learned something is worth more than a thing which hasn't.

It's in our cellars, and she wants to know what it has read.

ud_colonnade_dalaran.description: There's Dalaran masonry in the Weeping Colonnade, worked violet stone with Kirin Tor jointing and columns standing in courses. It's two hundred spans below the Ruins of Dalaran, in a cavern three years old. The Codex found it in their first month and have been very careful ever since to call it a find rather than a problem. Walk the colonnade, south of the gate, from the south end to where it stops, and bring me worked fragments off the revenants in it, because what's on the floor is rubble and what they carry was chosen. Look at the jointing while you're there, because the surface version of these columns is still standing up top with weather on it, and this one has none.
ud_colonnade_dalaran.accept_text: Bring me the pieces with the cleanest edges. Those are the ones I can match.
ud_colonnade_dalaran.turn_in_text:
That's all of them, and every one of them cut rather than broken.

The Codex's official position is that the masonry fell. Stone that falls two hundred spans doesn't land in courses. I've said this at three briefings and I'll say it at a fourth.

ud_colonnade_dissidents.description:
I'm not going to dress this up for you.

The Codex Dissidents were colleagues. They went out to the colonnade to settle an argument about the masonry, and they settled it in a direction the rest of us didn't follow, and what came back wasn't interested in discussing it. They still wear the crimson. Some of them still carry their field books. I've read two, and I wish I hadn't.
ud_colonnade_dissidents.accept_text: If you find a field book on any of them, bring it back unread. I'll decide whether anyone else sees it.
ud_colonnade_dissidents.turn_in_text:
Thank you for not asking me which of them I knew.

The field books you brought back are in the same hand they always were, and that's the part the Codex won't look at. Their minds are perfectly clear. They're writing clearly, and what they're writing is wrong.

ud_dawn_skitterers.description:
Clear the Crystalback Skitterers off the shelf. I've lost two sighting glasses this month, and the Codex's position is that I should be more careful with Codex property.

They aren't aggressive so much as curious, which makes no difference to the glass. Work the scree at the shelf edge. That's where they nest, and they don't go far from it.
ud_dawn_skitterers.accept_text: If you find a glass in the scree, bring it back. I'd like to put it on the Codex's desk myself.
ud_dawn_skitterers.turn_in_text: It's quieter now. I can hear my own chronometer again, which matters more than it sounds. I'm timing the Lumen, I've been doing it for three years, and it hasn't drifted by a minute.

ud_dim_edge.description:
Go to the boundary and a little over it, but not far over. I want somebody else's description of the first two hundred paces, because I've given mine four times and I don't trust it any more.

The light doesn't fade going in, it just stops. You'll be able to put a hand across the line and have one of them lit. Everything I've learned about what lives past it, I learned going the other way.
ud_dim_edge.accept_text: Count your paces as you go. I want the number, not just your impressions.
ud_dim_edge.turn_in_text:
You came back walking. That puts you ahead of me.

And you saw the line. Everyone describes the same line. Light doesn't do that. It falls off, it doesn't hold an edge, so something is holding it, and it's holding it from the dark side.

ud_dim_walkers.description:
Go after the Dim-walkers. Take them at the boundary rather than hunting them inward. Inward is how I lost a partner.

They won't cross into the light while you're watching. I've sat out there for whole shifts and they don't cross. Turn your back for the length of a slow count and they're thirty paces nearer, still in the dark, and the dark is in a different place than it was.
ud_dim_walkers.accept_text: Keep your face to the dark the whole time. Don't give them the slow count.
ud_dim_walkers.turn_in_text:
That's them off the line.

It'll be quiet for about a week. It always is. Then there'll be one standing out there again at the start of a shift, and I won't have seen it arrive.

ud_first_sight.description:
Walk out to the edge of the shelf and look at it properly. That's the whole task, and I won't pretend otherwise.

Everyone who comes down that passage expects a cave. What they get is a country with a lid on it, and the adjustment takes a few minutes. Have yours here, where the ground is flat, rather than halfway down the slope with something chewing on you.
ud_first_sight.accept_text: Sit down if you need to. Half the people who come out here do, and nobody here will say anything.
ud_first_sight.turn_in_text:
So now you've seen it.

The Codex has eleven thousand entries, and not one of them is any use to a person standing where you just stood. Go on down, and take my advice. Pick the light and walk at it, and you won't get lost in here.

ud_lattice_measure.description: If the Lattice were grown, it would vary, because stone varies and ice varies and bone varies. I've measured eleven sites across the field, and the figure repeats to a tolerance I can't tell from exact. I need a twelfth from the far side of the field, past the standing figures, where the growth is oldest and nobody goes because the sentries are thickest. Bring me shard cores from there, and the position, because I need to know where you stood and not just what you brought back. Take the long way round the central mass, because I'd rather have the reading late than not at all.
ud_lattice_measure.accept_text: Count your paces from the last standing figure. That's the position I'll write down.
ud_lattice_measure.turn_in_text:
That's the twelfth site, with the same figure at the same tolerance.

Eleven thousand entries in the Codex, and not one column for things that were made. I've started keeping my own book.

ud_lattice_repeats.description:
Go after the sentries, and I want them taken apart rather than simply dropped. Cut them where the figure closes. You'll see it, because there's a seam in the pattern and it's always in the same place relative to the body.

If it's in the same place on all of them, I can stop calling it mineralisation. Then it's a design, and designs have designers, and I'll put that in a report whatever the Codex rules.
ud_lattice_repeats.accept_text: Sketch the seam for me if you can. I'd rather see your drawing than hear your description.
ud_lattice_repeats.turn_in_text:
It's the same seam at the same offset on all of them, to within a finger's width.

I'm going to write the word manufactured and sign it, and then I expect I'll be having a conversation with the Codex-Master.

ud_marsh_glimmerjaw.description:
Kill all the Glimmerjaws, and work the deep channels rather than the banks. The bank fish are young, and they aren't what's taking my markers.

Don't follow the light. The lure sits well forward of the animal, and people who swim toward it meet the rest of it on the way.

The Lumen Marsh is east of the Bastion's gate, where the light comes up out of the water.
ud_marsh_glimmerjaw.accept_text: Wade slowly in the channels. Splashing tells them where you are.
ud_marsh_glimmerjaw.turn_in_text:
And my markers?

Then they aren't taking the markers for the light. Something in the marsh is taking them because they're markers, and I'd very much like to be wrong about that.

ud_marsh_timekeeping.description: The Lumen Marsh glows from underneath, and the glow brightens and fades on a cycle that matches the great light overhead to within a few minutes. I've timed it for two years. A cave has no reason to have an opinion about time, and this one keeps better time than the Codex's chronometers. Go to the marsh, east of the Bastion's gate, and bring me lumen sacs off the leeches in the shallows, taken at low lumen when the water is dim. If sacs cut an hour apart all show the same phase, then the water is only keeping time with something else, and so are we.
ud_marsh_timekeeping.accept_text: Mark the hour on each one as you cut it. Without that, the light tells me nothing.
ud_marsh_timekeeping.turn_in_text:
They all show the same phase.

There's a clock in this cavern and none of us built it. Three years we've set our watches by the Lumen and called it convenient.

ud_reach_husks.description:
Go after the Mycelial Husks out in the Reach, where the threads run thickest. I'll tell you plainly what I think you're doing, because you'll work it out yourself and I'd rather you heard it here. Those were people, or they were something that walked.

The growth didn't kill them for food. It kept the shape. It kept the shape and put itself inside it, and I don't have a word for what that's called when a plant does it.
ud_reach_husks.accept_text: Don't pull the threads out after. Let them be where they've grown.
ud_reach_husks.turn_in_text:
Did any of them still have belongings?

I asked that of the last four people I sent, and I've got four different answers, which means I'm going to have to go and look myself.

ud_riftward_geometry.description:
Go out to the far edge, and bring me samples of the residue off whatever is standing there. Then come back and tell me how many sides it had.

I'm not going to tell you my own figure. If I tell you my figure you'll see my figure, and that's precisely the error I'm trying to rule out.

The Dim Reaches are south-west of the Bastion, past the last of the lit galleries.
ud_riftward_geometry.accept_text: Count the sides twice, from two different places. If you get two answers, tell me both.
ud_riftward_geometry.turn_in_text:
That's a different number from mine, and from all four of the surveys.

That's good, though I want to be clear that it's a very bad result. It's the first honest one I've had out there.

ud_riftward_unfinished.description:
The Codex has filed the things out in the Riftward, north-east of here, as the Unfinished. Kill them, and I want you to watch what they do rather than simply end them. They cast the same spell twice and get two different results, and that isn't a mistake on their part. The spell is the same. The world it lands in hasn't settled.

If you can tell me which half is inconsistent, the caster or the ground, you'll have told me more than three years of Codex surveying has.
ud_riftward_unfinished.accept_text: Watch the ground where their spells land, not the casters. That's where I'd look.
ud_riftward_unfinished.turn_in_text:
So it's the ground, and you're certain.

That's the worse of the two answers, and I thought it would be. A caster that misfires is a bad caster. Ground that gives different answers to the same question doesn't deserve the name.

ud_shard_crates.description:
Bring me cores, and take them out of the lattice sentries rather than off the ground. Ground stock is half shell, and the Reagent-Keeper sends it back with a note.

The sentries will let you walk out there. They object when you start cutting. There's no way to do this politely, and I've stopped looking for one.
ud_shard_crates.accept_text: Cut close to the core and leave the shell. The Reagent-Keeper weighs everything.
ud_shard_crates.turn_in_text:
They're weighed, and I'll weigh them again at the gate.

If they come out lighter up there, it isn't you. It's been happening for a year, and the Codex's explanation is the scales.

ud_silver_bars.description:
I want bars. Dig it out of the fields yourself and smelt it yourself, because I'm not sending ore up to the Bastion so that a factor can take a cut of my own rock.

There's silver all through this plain. There's also iron, and coal in thin seams, so you won't be short of a fire. Bring me bars and I'll put your name in the ledger as a field hand, which is worth more down here than it sounds.
ud_silver_bars.accept_text: Stamp your mark on the bars if you've got one. I like to know whose work I'm selling.
ud_silver_bars.turn_in_text: That's all of them, and clean. You'll find most people down here can do one half of a trade. The Codex trains specialists and then puts them two hundred spans from anybody else's specialty.

ud_sporefall_caps.description:
Take the caps off the grazers out in the forest proper, not the little ones at the rim. The rim stock is stunted and the Codex's cooks can taste the difference, which I resent.

The ones that look like faces are fine, incidentally. Everybody asks about those. The stalks will put you on the floor for a day, so leave the stalks.
ud_sporefall_caps.accept_text: Keep them in the cool side of your pack. They bruise if they get warm.
ud_sporefall_caps.turn_in_text:
That's all of them, and two good enough to argue about.

You aren't from here either, are you? Nor am I, in the sense that matters. Everyone in this cavern walked in, which is the only thing I like about it.

ud_sporefall_drifters.description: The Spore-Drifters move in loose clouds between the great caps, and most of the time they're only a nuisance. For six weeks now they've been moving in the same directions at the same hours, and the hours line up with the Lumen's cycle. I've mentioned this to the Codex twice, and I've been thanked for my observation twice. Thin them out along the paths between the big caps, because that's where they drift and that's where my foragers walk. Mind the ones that are already clustered, because they share something between them and the rest of the cloud gets stronger the second you start on one.
ud_sporefall_drifters.accept_text: Break the clusters up before they close ranks, or you'll be fighting the whole grove at once.
ud_sporefall_drifters.turn_in_text:
You noticed the clustering, then. Everybody notices once something has used it on them.

A swarm doesn't behave like that. Swarms don't get stronger when you thin them. Something is feeding them instructions, and I've stopped saying so out loud.
